outcome: Live measurement of save and refresh latency on the household installation. Every second of a Stop Monitoring action is attributed. The server refresh cycle dominates: each save and each 60 s reconcile tick runs a full discovery of about 5.5 s on the event loop, and about 85 percent of that discovery is Home Assistant deprecation-frame inspection triggered by reading the deprecated DeviceEntry.config_entries property. The catalog reload after an edit costs a further 1.5 to 3 s.
plan: Homeostatic save and refresh latency investigation plan, phase 1 (observe the live house, no code changes)

measurements.stop_2_response_gap: the save finished on the server after 7.77 s but the client received it at 12.6 s; the reconcile tick queued behind the save ran its discovery for 4.6 s and the response was flushed only after it

ranking.B_full_catalog_reload: 15 to 23 percent of a Stop action (1.5 to 3.0 s for 63 pages), plus about 1 to 2 s of follow-up source reads and rendering; idle reconcile ticks did not bump catalog_revision

remaining_limits: One device, one browser on a Windows PC over the LAN; no phone or Safari timing
asyncio debug mode and cProfile inflate durations inside their windows; the six unprofiled cycles are the latency evidence
The regular pauses of about 1.0 s inside snapshot and checkpoint are unattributed; a garbage-collection pass is the working hypothesis and needs py-spy
The 8.7 s gap between server completion and client response in the profiled Stop is unattributed (profiling overhead and other integrations ran at the same time)
Medians come from three Stop and three Resume samples at different tick phases, short of the five-sample discipline the plan asks for in phase 3
